text:
maria: Observed a weird tail at p99 when enabling FlashAttn v3 on paged attention + KV cache. Latency spikes on long contexts (>= 8k) only after warm-up. Anyone else see this? :thinking:
ajay: Yep, saw it in the nightly run. Flamegraphs point to a kernel switch hot path + memory churn when page boundaries align with batch splits. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/2654321000 (access via vault) :eyes:
kevin: Quick summary from my side: v3 microbench shows better throughput bulk, but for paged cases we hit two issues: 1) KV cache eviction/reload cost overlaps with the attention kernel that assumes contiguous memory 2) batch packing causes fragmented GEMM shapes, triggering a different kernel variant with worse latency tail.
sara: Can we short-circuit to a stable kernel when seq_len > X or when page_miss_rate > Y? We should decide flag semantics for rollout.
ajay: Proposed flag matrix (draft):
```
attn_kernel_selector: 
  - default: adaptive_v3
  - fallback_rules:
      - if paged && seq_len >= 8192: use flash_v2_paged_fallback
      - if kv_miss_rate > 0.07: use flash_v2
      - if batch_fragmentation_score > 0.4: prefer fused_attention_legacy
```
kevin: That looks good. For the fragmentation score we can compute per-worker over 30s windows. Implementation detail: the selector needs to be cheap (<= 100 CPU ns) since it's called per-request.
perf-bot: nightly-bench results attached: avg token cost slightly lower on v3, but p95/p99 regressions on paged workloads:
```
Model A | seq=4096 | v2 p99=48ms | v3 p99=52ms
Model A | seq=8192 | v2 p99=92ms | v3 p99=125ms <-- regression
```
ops-bot: deploy 2654321010: rolled selector flag to staging (adaptive_v3 enabled). Canary monitors active.
maria: Important: the regression only manifests under dynamic batching with high variance in prefix lengths. Static batches are fine. So batching heuristic needs to be aware of page boundaries.
ajay: Agree. Two immediate mitigation options: 1) change batcher to avoid mixing differing page-aligned requests (pack by page_id) 2) bias the selector to use v2 for mixed-page batches. Both doable.
sara: Rollout plan suggestion:
- Stage (staging): enable adaptive_v3 on a shadow cluster, collect p95/p99, kv_miss_rate, fragmentation_score for 48h
- Canary 1% (production): enable with selector fallback rules from draft; watch p99 and error budget for 2h windows
- Ramp to 10% if stable, 4h observation windows.
- Post-ramp: enable autoswap where if p99 delta > +15% for 5m, auto-fallback to v2 for that route.
kevin: Also add a telemetry tag to identify requests that hit the fallback so we can correlate model+route+seq_len. Minimal schema: `attn_kernel=flash_v3|flash_v2|fallback` in traces.
maria: Can we also add a KV warm-up probe? Small cheap prefix decode to preload pages for high-latency tails. Might smooth the warm-up spike.
ajay: Good idea. We'll implement a configurable warm-up probe that runs when a route sees consecutive long-context requests and KV hit rate < threshold. Probe payload is tiny.
perf-bot: microbenchmark patch for page-aware batcher in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt/pull/701 (bench numbers optimistic but promising).
sara: Ops checklist for rollout: feature-flag timeline, canary monitors (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, kv_miss_rate, batch_fragmentation), runbook entries for auto-fallback triggers, owner oncall. Assign owners?
maria: I'll own the selector and metrics dashboards. Kevin, you take batcher changes. Ajay, you own the KV probe and microbench follow-ups. Sara, you coordinate rollout and oncall.
kevin: Ack. I'll create a short migration doc with config knobs and default values.
ajay: Will add a small telemetry ping (one-line) to perf pipeline so we can chart fragmentation score in Grafana.
maria: OK let's aim for staging flip tomorrow 09:00 UTC, 48h data capture, then canary the following day. Thanks all. :rocket:
